title: M.P. hooch tragedy: Wanted accused caught after brief encounter in Sagar
author: PTI
content_html:
A man wanted in connection with the hooch tragedy in Madhya Pradesh's Sagar district that recently claimed 16 lives was captured after a brief encounter with police early on Sunday (September 13, 2026), officials said.

VIDEO | Madhya Pradesh hooch tragedy: Wanted accused apprehended after brief encounter with police in Sagar district.

(Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/d8jp61yd2p) pic.twitter.com/o8oJoCdEIW

— Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) September 13, 2026

The 21-year-old accused, Shivanjay Rajput, who was carrying a bounty of ₹30,000, suffered a gunshot wound to his leg during the face-off, they said.

With this, the number of accused arrested in the case of spurious liquor consumption has gone up to 19, police sources said.

Mr. Rajput allegedly fired three rounds at a police team during a search operation near Kathua Nala forest area under Bahrol police station, following which the security personnel fired two rounds in retaliation and hit him in the leg, the officials said.

The accused was subsequently arrested and taken to a hospital for treatment. His condition was stable, Sagar police control room in-charge sub-inspector R.K.S. Chauhan told PTI over the phone.

Mr. Rajput, a resident of Chhapri village under Banda police station in Sagar, had been absconding since the spurious liquor incident earlier this month killed 16 persons. He was involved in brewing the liquor, and a reward of ₹30,000 was offered for information leading to his arrest, according to police.

A country-made .315-bore pistol, three live cartridges, three empty cartridges, a mobile phone and a motorcycle were recovered from his possession, a police statement said.

Police received information early on Sunday (September 13, 2026) that Mr. Rajput, who allegedly has three criminal cases registered against him and was previously involved in liquor smuggling, was in the forest near Kathua Nala and might pass through the Dhamoni-Bahrol road on his way home in Chhapri.

Following the tip-off, teams from Bandri and Bahrol police stations cordoned off the area and launched a search.

Mr. Rajput, who was on a motorbike, allegedly opened fire after spotting the police team, prompting retaliatory firing in which he was injured, the officials said.

Earlier, on Friday (September 11, 2026), one of the main accused in the Sagar hooch case, Ravi Lakhera was also captured after a brief police encounter. He was involved in 25 criminal cases and carried a reward of ₹30,000 on his head.

Mr. Lakhera, hailing from Lalitpur in Uttar Pradesh, was allegedly involved in manufacturing the spurious liquor.

The Sagar spurious liquor tragedy has claimed at least 16 lives so far since last week, with a patient in hospital still critical, an official said.

Police have claimed that a suspected gang from Lalitpur was linked to the manufacture and supply of the spurious liquor.

title: Calibrated capitulation: Congress slams PM Modi after his meeting with Xi
author: PTI
content_html:
The Congress on Sunday (September 13, 2026) posed four questions to Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his approach to India-China relations, and accused him of "calibrated capitulation" to that country.

Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh asked whether the PM's "infamous clean chit" to China on June 19, 2020, weaken India and why has he "allowed China's territorial advances in Ladakh and now Arunachal Pradesh".

Also read: BRICS summit LIVE updates

There was no immediate response from the government or the BJP over the Congress' claims.

Mr. Ramesh's remarks came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi conveyed to Chinese President Xi Jinping that peace and tranquillity along the frontier remains an "essential" basis for development of India-China relations, even as the two leaders welcomed "steady progress" in the bilateral ties.

In their talks on the sidelines of the BRICS summit, the two leaders reaffirmed that both the countries should take a strategic and long-term perspective of their ties and differences should not become disputes, according to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA).

In a statement posted on X, Mr. Ramesh said, "Now that his bilateral summit with President Xi Jinping is over, here are four questions for Prime Minister Narendra Modi to which the nation continues to seek answers. Did not your infamous clean chit to China on June 19, 2020 weaken India?" On the night of June 15-16, 2020, twenty of our soldiers made the supreme sacrifice in hand-to-hand combat with Chinese troops in the Galwan valley, the first such loss of life on the border in 45 years, the Congress leader recalled.

"Just four days later, on June 19, 2020, you inexplicably told an all-party meeting 'Na koi humari seema mein ghus aaya hai, na hi koi ghusa hua hai.' That statement has never been retracted. Has this not greatly weakened our subsequent negotiating position?" Mr. Ramesh said.

He further asked why has the PM "allowed China's territorial advances in Ladakh and now Arunachal Pradesh".

Our traditional patrolling and grazing rights across large stretches of Eastern Ladakh have been quietly but definitely "surrendered", he alleged.

Meanwhile, there have been reports of Chinese encroachment in Arunachal Pradesh, including loss of India's access to patrolling points and fresh standoffs, Mr. Ramesh claimed.

"China's posture on Arunachal Pradesh has only hardened: renaming towns, reasserting claims to what it calls 'South Tibet', and pushing ahead with its 60,000-MW Medog mega-dam on the Brahmaputra's Great Bend, a project that gives it a stranglehold over the water security of our entire northeast," the Congress leader said in his statement.

Why has the PM allowed softening of India's position on China's role in support of Pakistan during Operation Sindoor, Mr. Ramesh asked.

"On July 4, 2025, Lt. General Rahul Singh, the Deputy Chief of Army Staff, had publicly spoken of the military establishment's assessment of the deep and pivotal role of China in assisting Pakistan during Operation Sindoor. But all of a sudden, on August 25, 2026, the former Chief of Defence Staff Gen. Anil Chauhan took a completely different position in a lecture at the VIF with which the National Security Adviser has himself been closely associated. Was this part of a strategy to change the atmospherics leading up to yesterday's meeting?" the Congress leader said.

Why has the PM allowed the trade deficit with China to reach record levels, Mr. Ramesh asked.

India's trade deficit with China hit a record $112.6 billion in 2025-26, destroying large sections of our industry, especially MSMEs, he said.

"The dependence on China for critical raw materials, manufacturing components and intermediates has reached dangerous levels. 'Make in India' and 'Import from China' have become two sides of the same coin. Where is the roadmap for changing this unacceptable situation?" the Congress leader said.

"Prime Minister, normalisation of India's relations with China is one thing, but what has been in evidence on your part is calibrated capitulation," Mr. Ramesh said.

The MEA said that on the economic front, Mr. Modi and Mr. Xi underlined the need to address each other's concerns, including structural trade imbalance and supply chain issues, and facilitation of meaningful and predictable market access.

The two leaders expressed commitment to a "fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable" resolution of the boundary question proceeding from the political perspective of their overall bilateral relations and the long-term interests of the two sides, it said.

Mr. Xi's visit to India came on the heels of several high-level exchanges, including the Special Representative dialogue in Beijing between National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, even as lingering concerns remain over aggressive Chinese military posturing along the Arunachal Pradesh sector.

Mr. Modi and Mr. Xi held wide-ranging talks on August 31 last year on the margins of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in the Chinese city of Tianjin.

In the last few months, the two sides have taken a series of measures to rebuild their relationship after it came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020.

After over four years of frosty ties over the eastern Ladakh military standoff, India and China began to repair the relations following a meeting between Mr. Modi and Mr. Xi in the Russian city of Kazan in October 2024 that took place after the face-off ended.

Published - September 13, 2026 01:56 pm IST

title: The Security Council is paralysed, but the UN is not broken, says UNSG Guterres
author: Suhasini Haidar
content_html:
The Security Council is paralysed, and global superpowers haven’t recognized there are limits to their power says UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, in his most scathing comments about the culture of “impunity” and divisiveness that besets global leadership. In an exclusive interview to The Hindu on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS summit, the UNSG, who demits office at the end of the year, weighed in on a number of issues, including UN reform, the election for his successor, the latest developments in the West Asia war, Israel’s war in Gaza, India’s efforts in the Russia-Ukraine war, and the latest controversy of a new UN resolution on the world map.

title: BRICS Summit: PM Modi warns against weaponisation of technology, critical minerals
author: T.C.A. Sharad Raghavan
content_html:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (September 13, 2026) warned against the “weaponisation” of technology and critical minerals and also spoke about various BRICS initiatives agreed upon during the Summit in New Delhi to strengthen supply chains and increase resilience against supply-chain disruptions, pandemics, and climate disasters.

Also read: BRICS summit 2026 LIVE updates

While delivering the opening remarks on the second and final day of the BRICS Summit 2026, the Prime Minister noted that the number of conflicts and tensions in the world is continuously increasing, and that this is having an increasingly negative and far-reaching impact on the lives of ordinary people.

Later in the day, while delivering his closing remarks, the Prime Minister also said that, as BRICS enters its third decade, the world expects concrete results from them, not “merely ideas and commitments”.

Crisis preparedness

“The weaponisation of technology and critical minerals can hinder our shared progress,” Mr. Modi said. “Therefore, we have emphasised inclusivity in the adoption of technology. “Pandemics, climate disasters, and supply-chain disruptions have shown that in today’s interconnected world, no crisis remains confined to a single region.” 

Therefore, he said, the BRICS nations had placed special emphasis on strengthening resilience, with a focus on identifying challenges in time, being prepared for them, and taking prompt action.

“With this approach, we have agreed on a BRICS Integrated Early Warning System for the prevention of and response to infectious diseases,” Mr. Modi announced. “Early Warning Data Integration Guidelines have been prepared for disaster management. The BRICS Logistics Supply Chain Cooperation Framework will help make our supply chains more reliable and resilient.”

Focus on startups and tech

He added that the BRICS Incubator Network will connect start-ups and incubators in various BRICS nations with one another and that a BRICS Startup Innovation Fund has been proposed to promote innovative and scalable solutions.

“The BRICS Network on Digital Agriculture will create new opportunities for farmers,” Mr. Modi said. “Through this initiative, AI, geospatial technology, and Digital Public Infrastructure will be connected to the real needs of farmers.”

The Prime Minister also talked about BRICS CONNECT, aimed at promoting skills, employability, women in the workforce, social security, and capacity building.

“To connect small enterprises with knowledge, finance, and new markets, we have initiated the BRICS MSME Cooperation Portal,” Mr. Modi added. “The BRICS Urban Mobility Hub has been established to facilitate the sharing of best practices among our cities.”

Sustainability initiatives

Regarding the sustainability pillar of India’s strategy for BRICS, he said that a BRICS Digital Centre of Excellence has been established for smart grids and energy storage. 

“This will help make our clean energy systems more reliable, efficient, and accessible,” Mr. Modi said. The Centres of Excellence for Agro-Ecology and Regenerative Agriculture will connect traditional knowledge with modern science. The principles developed for community-based climate adaptation will make indigenous knowledge an important foundation for climate action.”

The Prime Minister also noted that, based on his personal experience, the Global South countries’ confidence in BRICS has grown because “their voices are heard, their experiences are respected, and solutions are developed not for them, but together with them”.

title: BRICS leaders voice concern over ‘growing risks’ of nuclear conflict
author: PTI
content_html:
BRICS leaders have voiced serious concern over "deliberate attacks" on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities under full safeguards of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), underlining that nuclear safety must always be upheld, including in "armed conflicts".

Also Read : BRICS Summit 2026 LIVE updates

In the ‘New Delhi Declaration’ adopted on the first day of the two-day BRICS Summit, being hosted by India, the leaders on Saturday (September 12, 2026) also expressed concerns over the "growing risks of nuclear danger and conflict".

Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the adoption of the declaration at the end of the opening day's deliberations in the presence of Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan and other top leaders of the bloc.

In a major diplomatic victory for India, BRICS reached consensus on the joint declaration after overcoming sharp differences between the United Arab Emirates and Tehran regarding the West Asia conflict, but skipped any direct mention of the U.S. strikes on Iran or the Iranian military's attacks on Gulf Arab nations.

The declaration, without naming any country, said, "We express serious concern over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities under full safeguards of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), in violation of international law and relevant resolutions of the IAEA," it said.

"Nuclear safeguards, safety, and security must always be upheld, including in armed conflicts, to protect people and the environment from harm," it added.

BRICS, comprising Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, expanded in 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Saudi Arabia, with Indonesia joining in 2025.

Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam became BRICS partner countries last year.

The declaration said, "We express concern about the growing risks of nuclear danger and conflict. We reiterate the need for invigorating the system of disarmament, arms control and non-proliferation and for preserving its integrity and effectiveness to achieve global stability and international peace and security."

The leaders also stressed the significant contribution of "nuclear-weapon-free zones" to the strengthening of the nuclear non-proliferation regime, reaffirmed their support for and respect towards all existing nuclear-weapon-free zones and their associated assurances against the use or threat of use of nuclear weapons.

They also acknowledged the importance of the efforts aiming at accelerating the implementation of the "resolutions on the Establishment of a Zone Free of Nuclear Weapons and other Weapons of Mass Destruction in the Middle East, including the Conference convened pursuant to UN General Assembly Decision 73/546."

"We call on all invited parties to participate in this conference in good faith and engage with this effort constructively. We note the adoption of the UNGA Resolution 79/241, ‘Comprehensive study of the question of nuclear-weapon-free zones in all its aspects’, as well as the successful conclusion of the study, which was adopted by the group by consensus," the declaration said.

title: BRICS 2026 beyond the Declaration: An Indian feast, Bollywood tunes by the Malaysian PM, and more
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The first day of the 18th BRICS Summit being held in New Delhi on Saturday (September 12, 2026) saw the grouping arrive at a crucial consensus, as negotiators worked until the last minute to bring Iran and the United Arab Emirates on the same page.

Also Read : BRICS Summit 2026 LIVE updates

The eagerly awaited New Delhi Declaration skipped direct mentions of the U.S. strikes on Iran or Iranian military’s attacks on several Gulf Arab nations, but called for “maximum restraint” in the war. It also made no separate mention of the Russian war in Ukraine.

With the diplomatic hurdles cleared early in the evening, the cohort returned to the decked-out Bharat Mandapam at night for the gala dinner. The newsmakers attending the Summit wrapped up the first day with an Indian feast, some Bollywood tunes, and much more.

Chinese President Xi Jinping skips gala dinner

Chinese President Xi Jinping skipped the gala dinner hosted by Mr. Modi, sources aware of the matter said. The reason for the absence of the Chinese President is not immediately known. Mr. Xi arrived in New Delhi on Saturday (September 12, 2026) afternoon and attended the BRICS Summit, besides having a fruitful bilateral meeting with Mr. Modi.

Abu Dhabi Crown Prince departs, Saudi FM arrives

The Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed, who left for home after attending the BRICS Summit during the day, was also a notable absentee at the high dinner table. Meanwhile, the Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan arrived in New Delhi as a late addition, soon after the departure of the Abu Dhabi Crown Prince

#WATCH | Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud arrives at the Delhi Airport to attend the BRICS Summit. pic.twitter.com/ngk6OpwwvI

— ANI (@ANI) September 12, 2026

Malaysian PM showcases love for Bollywood with Kishore Kumar song

Infusing a distinctive cultural resonance into his official visit to the national capital, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim blended statecraft with classic Bollywood melodies, spontaneously performing Kishore Kumar’s timeless track “Khwab Ho Tum Ya Koi Haqeeqat” from the 1965 film Teen Devian.

Guru mintak izin nyanyi kejap ok! pic.twitter.com/NzazFHV509

— Anwar Ibrahim (@anwaribrahim) September 12, 2026

Mr. Anwar, participating in the BRICS Summit, delivered the musical rendition during his stay at a Delhi hotel. The performance showcased the iconic composition by S.D. Burman alongside lyrics penned by Majrooh Sultanpuri, reflecting a long-standing personal appreciation for Hindi cinema that frequently surfaces during his diplomatic engagements.

‘Millet pulao’, ‘paneer lababdar’, ‘shahtoot phirni’: An Indian feast at the gala dinner

‘Paneer lababdar’, ‘gucchi marmik’, ‘millet pulao’, and ‘shahtoot phirni’ for desserts were among the Indian delicacies served to the leaders and delegates of the BRICS Summit at a gala dinner hosted by Mr. Modi at the Bharat Mandapam on Saturday (September 12, 2026). The menu included ‘khandvi mille’ and ‘khumb galouti’ as starters.

The other items that were offered include ‘thakkali belle saaru’ – light lentil broth of toor dal enriched with fresh tomatoes and curry leaves; ‘millet pulao’ – fragrant basmati rice and pearl millets cooked with spices and seasonal aromatics; ‘beetroot raita’ – chilled yoghurt with beetroot and fresh herbs; and assorted Indian breads.

Union Ministers, CMs attend BRICS gala dinner

The gala dinner also saw the Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, along with Union Ministers and Chief Ministers of various States in attendance.

The Union Ministers, including Amit Shah, Nirmala Sitharaman, Piyush Goyal, Ashwini Vaishnaw, Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Sarbananda Sonowal, and Kiren Rijiju travelled together in two buses from the Parliament House complex amidst tight security.

India is proud to host BRICS Summit 2026 under the leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister @narendramodi Ji. India welcomes #BRICS Leaders. Joining my colleagues and Chief Ministers at the Banquet hosted by Hon'ble Prime Minister for the visiting dignitaries. pic.twitter.com/BCG1eSVOFe

— Kiren Rijiju (@KirenRijiju) September 12, 2026

Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Chief Ministers of various States — Yogi Adityanath (Uttar Pradesh), Devendra Fadnavis (Maharashtra), Suvendu Adhikari (West Bengal), Himanta Biswa Sarma (Assam), Pushkar Singh Dhami (Uttarakhand), and Rekha Gupta (Delhi) — also travelled in the buses along with the Union Mnisters to the dinner venue Bharat Mandapam.

The Ministers were allotted different tables where delegates from different countries joined them during the dinner.

‘BRICS Symphony’: Ensemble of artistes from India, other countries perform at gala dinner

An ensemble of artistes drawn largely from India as well as other member countries of BRICS performed at a gala dinner.

A special cultural performance, Navarasa - The Universe of Shared Emotions, was presented during the #BRICS Leaders' Summit Gala Dinner hosted by the Prime Minister @narendramodi at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi yesterday evening.

The cultural event featured the BRICS Symphony -… pic.twitter.com/XaxY7QImoe

— All India Radio News (@airnewsalerts) September 13, 2026

Titled “Navarasa – The Universe of Shared Emotions”, the special cultural performance was presented during ahead of the gala dinner, in a celebration of the shared cultural heritage and diversity of the BRICS nations.

The cultural event also featured the BRICS Symphony – “One Rhythm, Many Cultures”, bringing together musicians from BRICS Members and Partner countries in a unique collaborative musical performance.

Friendship mural: At Summit venue, artists from BRICS member countries create ‘Sangam’ of cultures

 Inspired by the Indian concept of ‘Sangam’ — meeting of rivers — artists from various member countries of BRICS have come together to create a large-scale thematic mural at the Summit venue, symbolising friendship and a confluence of cultures.

Take a look at Sangam: A Confluence of Cultures; a large-scale collaborative public art project created by artists from 9 countries.

Inspired by the Indian concept of Sangam, where rivers from different origins meet and flow together, the artwork brings together artists and… pic.twitter.com/n1wCbZYjUx

— BRICS 2026 (@BricsIndia2026) September 11, 2026

The vibrant canvas, born out of the “BRICS Friendship Mural project”, is displayed on a wall inside the main Bharat Mandapam building, which houses the Summit Room, a senior official of the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), the cultural arm of the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), told PTI.

It was created under the theme “Sangam: Confluence of Cultures” and brings together the diverse artistic traditions of the BRICS member countries in a single collaborative public artwork.

India Post releases commemorative postage stamps to mark two decades of BRICS

 The Department of Posts on Saturday released two commemorative postage stamps to mark two decades of formation of BRICS, an official statement said.

A historic global moment, preserved forever through the timeless legacy of India Post 🇮🇳

Two Commemorative Postage Stamps marking the 18th BRICS Summit, New Delhi 2026, were released by Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, in the presence of… pic.twitter.com/4myCm1Qr5I

— India Post (@IndiaPostOffice) September 12, 2026

BRIC was formalised at the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York in 2006. Later, with the entry of South Africa into the bloc, the name was changed to BRICS.

The commemorative stamp bears the inscription ‘BRICS: Two Decades of Cooperation, 2006-2026’ in both English and Hindi.

title: U.P. top Shia leader pushes for stronger India-Iran ties in meeting with President Pezeshkian
author: Mayank Kumar
content_html:
Stressing the need to further strengthen India-Iran relations, Lucknow-based cleric and General Secretary of the All-India Shia Personal Law Board Maulana Yasoob Abbas on Saturday (September 12, 2026) said expanding cooperation between the two countries in education, trade, culture, science, technology, connectivity and energy is key for regional and global progress and prosperity.

“I met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in New Delhi on Friday (September 11) and called for further strengthening of the historic ties between India and Iran. I handed over a letter to the President of Iran, stressing the need to further strengthen India-Iran relations and condemning the attacks on Iran. India and Iran are two ancient civilisations with centuries-old cultural, intellectual, spiritual and trade relations. He stressed the need to further expand cooperation between the two countries in education, trade, culture, science, technology, connectivity and energy,” Mr. Abbas told The Hindu. 

Mr. Abbas welcomed President Pezeshkian on behalf of the Shia community in India and described his visit as an important opportunity to deepen friendship and understanding between the people of the two countries. I expressed hope that under President Pezeshkian’s leadership, India-Iran relations would enter a new and stronger phase.

“I expressed deep concern over the continuing tensions in West Asia and called for an immediate reduction in hostilities. I hope that the ongoing conflict will end soon and that peace and stability will return to the region. In my brief interaction, I expressed grief over the martyrdom of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Sayyid Ali Khamenei and strongly condemned the killing of innocent children, teachers and civilians in the attack on Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab. The killing of innocent children was a tragedy that had shaken the conscience of humanity,” said the Shia cleric. 

During the meeting, Mr. Abbas condemned terrorism, extremism and all forms of violence, and also denounced the attacks on Iran. “The people of India, particularly the Shia community, stand for peace, dialogue, humanity and justice. We urge our Iranian brothers to protect the interests of India and the Indian people in the West Asia region across land and sea, including the peaceful passing of ships with Indian flag,” he said.

title: M.A. Baby blames ‘creation of false perception’ for CPI(M)’s debacle in Keralam
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] national general secretary M.A. Baby has claimed that a “deliberate creation of false perception” against Left democratic forces among the masses had played a key role in the reverses suffered by the party in Keralam in recent times.

Opening a three-day extended State committee meeting of the CPI(M) on Sunday (September 13, 2026) morning, he also admitted that the Left should have been more alert in responding to the construction of this false perception. “We should have exposed this false narrative and defeated it, but we did not do it. There were some other lapses as well on our part. We need to correct these mistakes, regain the trust of the people and march forward,” Mr. Baby said.

The CPI(M) leader pointed out that regressive forces had been resorting to defaming the Communist forces for long. Recalling the ‘Liberation Struggle’, a popular agitation in the 1958-59 period supported by the Congress and other parties against the first democratically elected Communist government led by E.M.S. Namboodiripad in Keralam, Mr. Baby said it was actually a movement against the progressive steps piloted by the State.

“The construction of such false perceptions have continued since then. Though the Communist government was undemocratically dismissed by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1959, the vote share of the undivided Communist Party of India went down by 4% in the 1960 election. That shows how our policies influenced the people. However, because of the consolidation of anti-Left and right-wing forces, we could not come to power then,” he said.

Mr. Baby claimed that a similar situation happened in Keralam in 2026 too. “The creation of false perceptions against the CPI(M) and its leaders began after the party-led front came back to power in the 2021 Assembly polls. One among them is that we have reached a deal with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh and the Bharatiya Janata Party. That allegation has influenced a large number of people. We need to examine where we have made mistakes in countering such campaigns,” he said.

The CPI(M) leader said that the party cadre should engage in what he called criticism of others and of themselves. “Most of our prominent leaders, including some of those who are at the helm now, have gone through a rectification exercise by the party. We have a time-tested method for corrective steps,” he added.

The three-day conference is being held against the backdrop of the electoral reverses suffered by the CPI(M)-led Left Democratic Front in Keralam. The Central Committee of the party had earlier come out with a review report on the election performance. Based on it, the State committee has also prepared a set of guidelines to be followed by the cadre for the revival of party’s fortunes.

The participants at the conference, who also include district secretariat members of the party from across the State and leaders of its class and mass organisations, will discuss that document presented by M.V. Govindan on Sunday (September 13). The discussions will continue on Monday (September 14).

According to party sources, the State committee will prepare another report based on the outcome of the deliberations on September 15.

Earlier, senior party leader Paloli Mohammed Kutty raised a party flag. At least nine Polit Bureau members, including Mr. Baby, Mr. Govindan, and Opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan are attending the meeting.

title: Karnataka Minister Satish Jarkiholi says he was misquoted on ED searches; releases video message
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Satish Jarkiholi, Karnataka Minister and Congress leader, has said that he was misquoted by some media outlets in reports about the Enforcement Directorate searches at his premises.

“Some newspapers have reported that I have thrown a challenge to the ED to prove my overseas investment. This is far from truth. I have never said that,” he said in a video message. This is to clarify that I have not challenged ED or any other agency. I have not used that word anywhere. There is no question of posing any challenge to any agency.”

ED ಒಂದು ತನಿಖಾ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆ. ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಸವಾಲು ಹಾಕುವ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಯೇ ಇಲ್ಲ. ಆದರೆ ಪತ್ರಿಕೆಗಳು ಹಾಗೂ ಮಾಧ್ಯಮಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಕಟವಾಗಿರುವ ಕೆಲವು ವರದಿಗಳು ಸತ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ದೂರವಾಗಿವೆ.#SatishJarkiholipic.twitter.com/RariFlXyk3

— Satish Jarkiholi (@JarkiholiSatish) September 13, 2026

“There is no question of posing challenges to anyone, and I do not need to do such a thing. We are only working towards providing all documents to the ED regarding the issue. I have held three press conferences about the searches. I have repeatedly said that we are cooperating with the ED investigation and giving them all the records. However, some media outlets are reporting it in their own style that gives a wrong message to the general public and the concerned agency. What is more, such statements can be used against us. I therefore urge the media to report the facts and our statements as they are’’, he said in the message.
